analyst_view.overall: Early view: Manchester United are 18th in the Premier League after a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday, and director of football Jason Wilcox is due to decide on Michael Carrick's future during the break, so United could have a different manager by December. Leipzig are 30th on three points after a 3-2 home defeat by Manchester City. Matheus Cunha's red card against Roma (second yellow) should be served at Sporting on matchday 5, so he should be available here.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean higher: United's last two games finished 3-2 and 4-4, and Leipzig have conceded 11 in four league-phase games. Both defences are leaky, and both teams need the points.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, 6.2 of them United's. I see nothing to change that: United will push forward at home, but Leipzig's quick wide players (Nusa, Gruda) mean this will not be one-way traffic.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards. I lean higher: both teams are under pressure (United near the relegation zone at home, Leipzig needing points to stay in the race), and Cunha's dismissal against Roma showed how tense United's European nights have become. The 4-4 with Villa had only two bookings, so this rests on the stakes rather than recent card counts.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots. I lean slightly higher, given that United and Leipzig have both been open, chaotic sides in Europe this season. A change of manager at United would make this harder to read.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.4 shots on target. I keep it: both teams have enough attackers (Fernandes, Cunha, Mbeumo, and Leipzig's front three) to test the keepers, and neither defence has held firm lately.
